independent_solution: In A's frame v_BA = v_B - v_A. B is seen moving perpendicular to A's line, so the component of v_B along A's line (at 60 - 30 = 30 deg to it) equals v_A: v_B cos30 = 100 sqrt3 -> v_B = 200 m/s.
Across A's line: |v_BA| = v_B sin30 = 100 m/s (A has no perpendicular component).
B, 500 m away across A's line, closes the gap at 100 m/s: t0 = 500/100 = 5 s.

Rocket frame accelerates at +2 m/s^2 in gravity-free space, so each free ball has acceleration -2 m/s^2 relative to the rocket. Left ball: x1 = 0.3t - t^2; right ball: x2 = 4 - 0.2t - t^2 (m, from the left end).

Ignoring the walls, x2 - x1 = 4 - 0.5t = 0 at 8 s, but x1 = 0 again at t = 0.3 s: the left ball returns to the left wall long before, so it is at the left end (pressed there by the frame's acceleration).
The right ball reaches the left end when t^2 + 0.2t - 4 = 0 -> t = (-0.2 + sqrt(16.04))/2 = 1.90 s, i.e. about 2 s as an integer answer. The 8 s value requires ignoring the chamber wall.
questions.independent_answer: about 1.9 s, i.e. 2 (integer answer); 8 s is not physical because the first ball hits the left wall at 0.3 s

independent_solution: Full question read on pinned page 9. Ground velocity = velocity relative to water + water velocity (3 m/s east).
(a) Heading north: (3, 4) m/s -> 5 m/s at tan^-1(3/4) = 37 deg east of north.

(b) To reach B directly opposite, cancel the drift: 4 sin(phi) = 3 -> phi = sin^-1(3/4) = 48.6 deg (= tan^-1(3/sqrt7)) west of north; resultant speed sqrt(16 - 9) = sqrt7 = 2.65 m/s. (c) Crossing time = width/(northward speed): 4 > sqrt7, so case (a) is quicker.
questions.independent_answer: (a) 5 m/s at 37 deg east of north; (b) heading 48.6 deg (tan^-1(3/sqrt7)) west of north, speed sqrt7 m/s; (c) case (a) is faster
questions.official_answer: (a) 5 m/s at 37 deg to N; (b) (i) tan^-1(3/sqrt7) west of N, (ii) sqrt7 m/s; (c) in case (i) he reaches the opposite bank in shortest time

independent_solution: Take i north, j vertically up; rain ground velocity v_r = a i + b j. Relative to the girl: v_r - v_girl.
At 5 m/s rain appears vertical: a - 5 = 0 -> a = 5. At 10 m/s it appears at 45 deg to the vertical: |a - 10| = |b| -> b = -5 (falling).
v_r = 5 i - 5 j: speed 5 sqrt2 = 7.07 m/s, falling at 45 deg to the vertical towards the north.
questions.independent_answer: v_r = 5 i - 5 j m/s: 7.07 m/s at 45 deg to the vertical, towards north
